units.function: HTTP tests for anonymously serving a Company's stored logo through an active invitation token.
units.dependencyDirection: An anonymous bearer token resolves an invite and Company logo asset record; the route performs Company-scoped storage metadata/read calls and streams bytes to the client.
units.keyDataModels: Invite status/Company/token hash/expiry, logo asset Company/objectKey/contentType/byteSize/filename and storage head/get stream metadata.
units.lifecycle: A valid active invite authorizes lookup of its Company's logo; existing storage content is streamed with its MIME type, while a database record whose object is missing returns a specific 404 without reading it.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover anonymous invite-bound access, Company-scoped storage keys and metadata-before-read missing-object behavior. Missing are invalid/revoked/expired/accepted tokens, cross-Company asset mismatch, rate limiting, MIME and size allowlists, SVG/script content, Content-Disposition/X-Content-Type-Options/CSP, cache policy, range requests, streaming errors and malicious storage metadata.
units.designRationale: Provide branded onboarding before the invitee has a Company identity without making all Company assets public.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a warm branded human onboarding experience while keeping enterprise assets and identity boundaries isolated.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the narrow invite-scoped public-brand projection and Company-scoped storage lookup. Serve only preprocessed raster variants through a dedicated public asset ID, enforce type/size/security headers and cache rules, rate-limit access, never expose general asset keys and retain provenance/license metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: A bearer invite implicitly authorizes public asset access, but the test does not prove who approved that brand asset for publication or whether the invite's lifecycle immediately revokes cached/public access.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres route test for descending offset pagination over Company invitation history with an associated join-request projection.
units.dependencyDirection: An implicit local board actor requests one Company path; access routes join persisted Company invites and join requests, sort and page them into an administrative response.
units.keyDataModels: Company, invite ID/type/tokenHash/join type/default role/expiry/timestamps and join request ID/type/status/IP/email snapshot, limit/offset/nextOffset.
units.lifecycle: Three persisted invitations are returned newest-first in two pages; an invitation with a pending join request includes its relatedJoinRequestId and the final page returns no next offset.
units.testAssessment: A real database validates ordering, pagination and relationship projection. It does not test permission denial, cross-Company access, invalid/large/negative paging, stable tie ordering, concurrent inserts, redaction of tokenHash/IP/email/default secrets, revoked/accepted status, N+1 behavior or audit access. Services are mocked and the board actor has no accountable user ID.
units.designRationale: Give administrators an operational history of onboarding links and their resulting requests.
units.companyOsProblem: Agent Boss and enterprise administrators need an auditable human/Agent admission ledger without exposing invitation secrets or personal data broadly.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the combined invite/join projection and newest-first cursor UX. Company OS should use cursor pagination, explicit users:invite or joins:approve authorization, row-level organization isolation, field-level PII/secret redaction and immutable admission/audit events rather than treating an implicit board as sufficient.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test's board actor has userId null, and no assertion proves who is allowed to see request IP/email or whether tokenHash is excluded. A related request ID is operational linkage, not a complete inviter/approver/identity-binding responsibility chain.

units.function: Anonymous invitation route tests for server-side reachability probing of a proposed public Agent gateway URL with extensive SSRF address filtering and DNS-pinned HEAD requests.
units.dependencyDirection: A bearer invite token, arbitrary URL and timeout enter access routes; the route verifies invite state, resolves DNS through an injected network layer, rejects forbidden address classes and passes the approved hostname plus pinned addresses to a HEAD requester.
units.keyDataModels: Agent invitation state, requested URL/timeout, DNS address family/list, pinned resolvedAddress/resolvedAddresses/Host/TLS server name and reachable/httpStatus response.
units.lifecycle: Missing, revoked or expired invites fail before DNS. Literal or resolved loopback, RFC1918, link-local metadata, multicast, NAT64/reserved and any mixed private answer fail before connection. An all-public HTTPS target is probed with a pinned address, original Host/SNI and bounded timeout.
units.testAssessment: Strong adversarial coverage includes IPv4-mapped IPv6, NAT64, mixed DNS answers, pre-lookup invite gating and connection pinning. Missing are scheme/port allowlists, redirects, repeated/rebinding resolutions, IDNA and exotic literals, proxy behavior, response size/body avoidance proof, connection timeout bounds, rate/concurrency limits, audit, domain ownership and authorization beyond possession of a bearer invite.
units.designRationale: Help an external Agent gateway validate connectivity during onboarding without exposing obvious private-network SSRF paths.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe FDE/Connector diagnostics and a data-egress firewall, but network probes are privileged execution actions rather than anonymous onboarding conveniences.
units.companyOsFit: Reject the anonymous invitation surface. Preserve the DNS classification and connect-to-pinned-IP technique inside an authenticated local execution node or FDE diagnostic workflow, constrained by organization egress policy, approved destination/port, rate and timeout budgets, responsible-human authority and durable evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Any bearer invite holder can make the server probe arbitrary public infrastructure. No human/organization policy approves the destination, no Connector binding or data contract exists, and the response becomes an unauthenticated network oracle even though private ranges are blocked.
